title: Bridgework: contribution contract, RFC pipeline, and retirement signals
creator: Amina Patel
description: Create a lightweight, auditable contribution contract and RFC pipeline for the design system that clarifies acceptance criteria for tokens and components, defines signal-based retirement triggers, and standardizes reviewer roles across Design/Engineering/PM. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc changes, shorten review cycles, and make component retirements predictable and observable for dependent product teams.
rationale: We currently have inconsistent contribution practices: some component PRs are effectively design-only, others require deep infra changes. Without a clear contract we see regressions, duplicated primitives, and surprise deprecations. A formal but lightweight pipeline will improve discoverability, reduce rework, and provide measurable signals for safe retirements.
scope: This covers all visual tokens (color, spacing, type scale), core interactive primitives (buttons, inputs), and data-display patterns (tables, charts, lists). It defines the RFC path for new components and the retirement signal taxonomy for existing ones. It does not change runtime APIs or SDK surface-level breaking changes handled by eng change controls.
out_of_scope: Low-level serving/runtime changes, private customer custom component repos, and post-migration engineering work. Also not changing legal or licensing processes.
acceptance_criteria: Contribution contract doc published in Confluence with clear checklist
RFC template merged in the design-system repo and linked from README
Review checklist adopted by design reviewers and engineering reviewers (2 approvers: one design + one eng for core primitives)
Retirement signal taxonomy defined with 3 measurable signals and associated thresholds
Sample retirement pilot executed on one low-usage token with migration notes and dashboard showing expected impact
review_checklist: Has the PR filled the RFC template and linked a Confluence design spec (if UI behavioral change)?
Is there a token mapping (old -> new) and migration plan for dependent repos?
Performance and accessibility impact assessed (a11y checklist completed)?
Engineering reviewer ran the component on canary build and verified visual regression diffs?
Design reviewer confirmed token usage and visual parity across documented examples?
Backward compatibility notes and fallback strategies documented for a 90-day window?
Telemetry hooks and dashboards proposed for post-release monitoring?
deprecation_policy_summary: Components and tokens will follow a staged deprecation: soft deprecation (warning in docs, migration guide) -> monitored deprecation (disabled in default bundles, telemetry monitored) -> hard removal (removed from main library after thresholds met). Default notice period is 90 days, can be extended for high-customer-impact items.
retirement_triggers: Usage threshold: < 0.5% of production renders across recent 30 days
Quality signal: repeated regressions or accessibility failures after attempted fixes
Duplication signal: canonicalized replacement landed and >75% of active repos adopted replacement
migration_guidance: Provide code snippets for common frameworks (React hooks, vanilla JS, CSS tokens)
Offer automated codemods for the highest-volume callers during pilot
Maintain an explicit mapping table in the Confluence page with examples before retiring
Design tokens: include both token alias and semantic intent to aid automated replacement
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish contribution contract and RFC template; announce in #design-system
Week 1-2: Run 2-hour office hours with engineering to walk through checklist and PR examples
Week 3: Pilot retirement on low-risk spacing token; enable telemetry dashboards
Week 4-8: Iterate on checklist based on pilot feedback and promote policy to "team-of-record"
Post-release: Quarterly reviews of retired items and any retro learnings
communication_plan: Announcement doc in Confluence and short email to product engineering leads
Pinned digest in #design-system + cross-post to #product and #infra
Release notes entry with migration guide and codemod links
Office hours recordings stored in Drive and linked from the RFC
decision_record: Opted for a lightweight RFC template (max 2 pages) to avoid process friction — 2025-09-24
Two-approver policy for core primitives (one design, one eng) approved by design leadership — 2025-09-26
Telemetry-driven retirement preferred over time-only schedules to avoid accidental breakage — 2025-09-29
